# Counter schema

The counters ffimap reports: what each one holds, how a record is shaped, and
how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
and no dataflow is performed.

What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is
[`analysis.md`](analysis.md); the ffibox vocabulary the `<trait>` and
`<primitive>` arms are generated from is [`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md).

## 1. The counters

Each row below is one counter, named by its dotted path into the document's
`counts`. A `{a,b}` is a split the counter carries: `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}`
is two leaves, and every row's leaves are integers. Each partition also carries
a `total`, derived from its children unless the driver emits it, so
`raw_ptr.field.total` exists and `raw_ptr.field.pub + raw_ptr.field.priv`
equals it; the `of_which` rows are shares of the row above them and are never
summed ([2.1](#21-partitions-and-shares)).

The counters are the whole of the document's `counts`. There is no second,
flat counter block beside them, and no prose rendering of them: a reader who
wants a rate divides the leaves it names.

Across the tree, `unsafe` and `safe` are the safety of the *function* the
position or site is in, `pub` and `priv` whether a consumer of the crate can
reach the item, and `void` a pointer whose pointee is erased (`*c_void`). A row
naming `ffibox`, a `<trait>` or a `<primitive>` is present only under
`--ffibox`, an `of_which.seam` row only with `--seams`, and a `region` or
`outside_regions` row only with `--regions`; each is absent rather than zero
otherwise ([2.3](#23-zero-and-absent)). A row ends with the property it bears
on, as [goals.md](goals.md) names them: safety, soundness, ergonomics or
idiomaticity.

content.content:
## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

## Planning
method; the pp cells are against this run's own tip measurement. The tip's `unit` count was
902, not the recorded 900. The C suites' shifts, `+0.04` pp in `ub_safe` and `-0.02` pp in
`unit`, which this batch's tests do not run, are run-to-run variation. Worklist: Rust
`strnlen_h.rs` 5 of 5 lines, 5 of 5 regions and 1 of 1 function; C `git__strndup`'s
`p_strnlen` line reached 109k times by `equiv`; `strnlen` itself is glibc's, outside the
archive. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total` (`+7`) and
`code.tests.loc.total` (`+100`).

The safety audit scans (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, `--ffibox`, `--sys-crates pcre2_sys`, the raw
bindings being the crate's own `sys` module since 2026-11-13, the 13 seams with `into_raw`,
`--regions ffi_import,ffi_export`, no export feature in the manifest) move only the line
totals; the boundary scan's sites hold none in the changeset. `ffimap api` against the tip,
with ffibox's private rustdoc JSON (nightly `2026-10-08`): `mac::p_strnlen` is `new`, and
every unattributed module `kept`.

Gates, on the base `50c93dd23`, which the wave branch still pointed at when the batch landed:
the workspace is formatted, and `clippy --all-targets` passes with warnings denied on
`plain`. The whole workspace passes on `plain` (`lib` 840 and 1 ignored, `ub_safe` 762,
`ub_unsafe` 120, `equiv` 528, `unit_pub` 67, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 72 merged and 378 standalone). The module's tests pass
under ASan+UBSan, and the six unit tests under Miri; the two `equiv` tests were each run alone
there and stop at `git_libgit2_init` (`calls libgit2`). The coverage runs ran every suite of
both trees on the nightly; only the known `CommitBuilder` compile-fail doctest fails, on both.
TSan and BSan have no obligation: the batch adds no unsafe code, no `Send` or `Sync` claim and
no thread. No raw binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. Usage cells are
the assistant's.

### `libgit2/src/util/strnlen.h` wave 225 batch 1: module pass

The module pass, and the module's only review, over batch 0's three paths, for every objective
with `fix`. It files no finding. `strnlen` is `p_strnlen`'s length for every input: the slice
is the pointer and its bound, and `CStr::from_bytes_until_nul` is core's `memchr`, a byte loop
below 16 bytes and word-wise above, as the docs say. It is `const`, safe and anchored
`Replaces` `mac::p_strnlen` with its alias, and no Rust in the crate counts a bounded length by

# An anchor's alias that equals its item's name

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent had to work out by hand that a skill should have stated: an annotation the
conventions require does not compile.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-1/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) ported the static function
`support_gnu_style`. The conventions' Naming section keeps a C name that already reads as a
Rust one (`snake_case`, no library prefix to drop), and their Anchors section puts
`#[doc(alias = "support_gnu_style")]` beside the `Replaces` anchor. On Rust 1.100.0 rustdoc's
check, which `cargo build` runs on every item, rejects it:

```text
error: `#[doc(alias = "support_gnu_style"]` is the same as the item's name
   --> src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs:102:15
```

The batch renamed the port `uses_gnu_style`, which a Rust caller reads as the predicate it
is, and kept the alias, so that a search of the docs for the C name still finds it. The
anchor alone would have recorded the translation, since a search by the item's own name
finds the item without an alias, but `ffimap` counts a wrapper by its `doc(alias)`
(`fn.ffibox.wrapper.*`) and `ffimap api` keys items by their anchors; neither was checked
for an anchor without its alias.

Any C function, global or macro whose name is already a valid, unprefixed Rust name meets
it: the CLI's static helpers (`opt.c`'s `spec_included`, `consume_choices`,
`validate_required`, `parse_long`, `parse_short`, `parse_arg`, `sort_gnu_style`, and the
`cmd_*.c` helpers) among them.

## Destination

The spec: the conventions' Anchors section (`rust/conventions`), which the translator and
binder do not evolve.

## Change

Add, after the paragraph on the alias:

> rustdoc rejects an alias equal to its item's name. A stand-in whose Rust name would equal
> its C name is therefore named otherwise, by the Naming section's rules, the idiomatic Rust
> term preferred, such as a predicate's `is_`, `has_` or `uses_` form, so that the alias, and
> the search it serves, is kept on every annotated item.

## Validation

`wave-186/batch-1/run-1` builds with the rename and the alias kept; with the alias equal to
the name the library fails to build (above).
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: sys.exit(r.stderr[-2000:])
    lines=r.stdout.splitlines()
    if srcs and not cd:
        roots=[str(pathlib.Path(d).resolve()) for d in srcs]
        rows=[l.split()[0] for l in lines[2:] if l.strip() and not l.startswith(('-','TOTAL','Filename'))]
        stray=[f for f in rows if not any(str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve()).startswith(r+'/') or str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve())==r for r in roots)]
        if stray: sys.exit(f'scope {srcs} reports {len(stray)} files outside it, such as {stray[0]}: its filters match no source')
    t=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('TOTAL')][-1].split()
    # TOTAL regions missed cover functions missed exec lines missed cover branches missed cover
    return dict(lines=(int(t[7])-int(t[8]),int(t[7]),t[9]),functions=(int(t[4])-int(t[5]),int(t[4]),t[6]),regions=(int(t[1])-int(t[2]),int(t[1]),t[3]))

Here's where things stand. My two items are ported and tested, but nothing has landed yet: the work depends on batch-0's enum types, so it has to land after batch-0 does.

**Both items depend on the enums, against the task's assumption.** `spec_is_option_type` compares a spec's `type` with three `cli_opt_type_t` constants. `support_gnu_style` tests two `cli_opt_flag_t` constants. Wavefront records neither edge, a gap already filed as `wavefront-enum-constant-uses`. As you asked, I haven't bound the enums myself. I wrote against stand-ins that mirror batch-0's in-progress `Kind` and `ParseFlags`. Once batch-0 lands, I rebase, delete the stand-ins and land on its real types.

**What's written so far** (committed only on my own branch, as a work-in-progress commit):
- **The macro** is ported as `Kind::is_option`, a `const fn` that is true for `Bool`, `Switch` and `Value`. The C parser has a long-option branch for accumulators that this check makes unreachable. No CLI spec uses an accumulator, so I kept the C behaviour and noted it in the docs.
- **The function** is ported as `uses_gnu_style(ParseFlags) -> bool`. I couldn't keep the C name: rustdoc refuses a doc alias equal to the item's name, and the conventions require the alias.
- **Raw bindings:** I allowlisted `cli_opt_parser_init` and `cli_opt_parser_next` for the equivalence tests. Batch-0 also edits the allowlist, so the rebase will conflict there; I'll merge both lists and regenerate.
- **Tests:** six `unit_pub` tests and two `equiv` tests compare against the C through those two parser functions. The macro is checked over 254 lists of spec types. The `POSIXLY_CORRECT` cases run in child processes, so no test changes its own process's environment. All of these pass plain and under ASan/UBSan. Miri is still running.

**`getenv` confirmation:** `std::env::var_os` holds as recommended. The C only checks whether `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set, and an empty value counts as set; `var_os(..).is_some()` matches that exactly.

**Proposals so far:**
- I filed `doc-alias-equal-to-the-name` against the conventions' Anchors section, which I don't own.
- I appended this case as later evidence to `wavefront-enum-constant-uses`.

**Still to do:** finish Miri, rebase onto batch-0, run the gates again plus coverage, the ffimap scans and packaging, fill the dashboard rows, then land under the landing lock.

content.content:
# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition

# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`

private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses

# The packaging gate's command is worked out by hand

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A procedure I had to work out by hand, over three failed runs, that the gate names but does
not give.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-0/run-1` changed the raw bindings (`sys/git2/allowlist.txt`). Per
`testing-gates`' Regressions section, that means it packages the safe crate "built alone in
bundled mode … each crate the package depends on … patched to its local source". Run from
the worktree with `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=` and `--allow-dirty`:

1. `cargo package` failed: `no matching package named glibc-bindings found` (crates.io). The
   manifest's `[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/…"]` does not apply to the packaged
   manifest, whose dependencies are registry ones. The fix was
   `--config 'patch.crates-io.glibc-bindings.path="/target/glibc-crustify"'
   --config 'patch.crates-io.ffibox.path="/crustify-rs/ffibox"'`.
2. The bundled CMake configure then failed: `PCRE2 support was requested but not found`, and
   after that `system zlib was requested but not found`. The side campaigns' installs
   (`<repo>/../{openssl,pcre2,zlib}-bindings/crustify/builds/plain/install`) have to be on
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, and colon-separated, since that is the environment variable's form.
   The `plain` variant's `configure` in `build.json` passes them semicolon-separated, as a
   `-D` value, and copying that form failed.

With both changes, the crate packaged 698 files and verified.

## Destination

A campaign artifact the assistant owns: a script beside `crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh`
(such as `crustify/scripts/package.sh`) that runs the gate with the patches derived from the
manifest's `[patch]` sections and the side installs from `build.json`'s `plain` prefix path.
Its use would then go in `testing-gates`' Regressions section, or in a lesson until the
wrappers are published.

## Change

Not made: neither file is the translator's. The command that passed:

```bash
S=$(realpath -m crustify/builds/plain/../../../..)
I() { echo "$S/$1-bindings/crustify/builds/plain/install"; }
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=$(I openssl) \
CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(I openssl):$(I pcre2):$(I zlib)" \
PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(I pcre2)/lib/pkgconfig:$(I zlib)/lib/pkgconfig" \
cargo package --allow-dirty \
  --config 'patch.crates-io.glibc-bindings.path="/target/glibc-crustify"' \
  --config 'patch.crates-io.ffibox.path="/crustify-rs/ffibox"'
```

## Validation

The command above packaged and verified the tree of `wave-186/batch-0`. The two earlier
forms failed as quoted.

## Review

None yet.

T=$W/crustify/tmp/wave-186-batch-1; L=$T/logs/g; rm -rf $L; mkdir -p $L

step() { echo "== $1 $(date +%T)" >> $L/progress; }

step clippy; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings > $L/clippy.log 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" >> $L/clippy.log
step plain;  cargo test --no-fail-fast > $L/plain.log 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" >> $L/plain.log
step asan;   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh asan-ubsan test --lib --test unit_pub --test equiv -- cli > $L/asan.log 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" >> $L/asan.log
step asandoc; crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh asan-ubsan test --doc -- cli::opt > $L/asan-doc.log 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" >> $L/asan-doc.log

(cd /crustify-rs/ffibox && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$T/ffibox-target cargo +$N rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json --document-private-items) > $L/rustdoc-ffibox.log 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" >> $L/rustdoc-ffibox.log
cp $T/ffibox-target/doc/ffibox.json $T/ffibox.json

### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` wave 186 batch 0: `opt.h`'s enums

The first batch of the `git2` link unit, the CLI. It ports `src/cli/opt.h`'s four enums into
`src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, as native Rust that keeps C's values. `enm::cli_opt_type_t` is
`Kind` and `enm::cli_opt_status_t` is `Status`: closed enums, as the plan judges them (their
doctest fails, on both trees. TSan and BSan have no obligation: there is no unsafe code, no
`Send` or `Sync` claim and no thread. The raw bindings changed, so the crate was packaged in
bundled mode (698 files) and verified. That took the unpublished wrappers patched on
`crates-io` and the side campaigns' installs on `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, colon-separated
(`crustify/evolution/packaging-gate-procedure`). Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` wave 186 batch 1: `spec_is_option_type` and `support_gnu_style`

The wave's symbol route: the TU-local macro `mac::spec_is_option_type` and the static function
`fn::support_gnu_style`, ported as native Rust into `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, beside batch 0's
enums. Both use those enums' constants, which wavefront records no use of
(`crustify/evolution/wavefront-enum-constant-uses`, whose evidence this batch extends): the
macro compares a spec's `type` with `CLI_OPT_TYPE_BOOL`, `_SWITCH` and `_VALUE`, and the function
tests `CLI_OPT_PARSE_FORCE_GNU` and `CLI_OPT_PARSE_GNU`. The batch was written against stand-ins
of batch 0's in-progress types and rebased onto its landing, `8a149ac08`, where it takes `Kind`
and `ParseFlags`. `spec_is_option_type` is `Kind::is_option`, a `const fn` over the spec's kind,
which a ported spec's kind answers; the C parser's long-argument branch for an accumulator stays
unreachable, as in the C, and no spec of the CLI is one. `support_gnu_style` is
`uses_gnu_style(ParseFlags) -> bool`: rustdoc refuses an alias equal to its item's name, so the
port is renamed and keeps the alias (`crustify/evolution/doc-alias-equal-to-the-name`). It reads
`POSIXLY_CORRECT` through `std::env::var_os`, libc's `getenv` taking its recommended `std` route,
which held exactly: the C tests presence alone, the empty value included. Nothing is exported:
no C outside `opt.c` reaches either item. The file keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. The
`loc` cell is wavefront's `query dag --loc`, `0` for the macro and `18` for the function.

The `git2` allowlist gains `cli_opt_parser_init` and `cli_opt_parser_next`, which the
equivalence tests reach the C through, and the bindings were regenerated in campaign mode,
833 lines: the two functions, `cli_opt_spec`, `cli_opt` and `cli_opt_parser`, whose bitfields
bring bindgen's `__BindgenBitfieldUnit`. Those helpers and `cli_opt_parser`'s `*_raw`
accessors are the safety audit row's `+10` public `unsafe fn`s, `+30` raw dereferences and `+37`
unsafe blocks, all in the generated `sys/git2/bindings.rs`; the safe crate's own counts do not
move, and the boundary scan's sites hold none in the hand-written changeset.

Tests: six `unit_pub` tests (the kinds a long name selects, the predicate in a `const` block,
`FORCE_GNU`, the default, unnamed flag bits, and `GNU` under `POSIXLY_CORRECT` unset, `1`, empty
and `0`, each in a child process of the test binary, since setting the environment is unsafe
beside the harness's threads), two `equiv` tests and two doctests. The equivalence of the macro
goes through `cli_opt_parser_next`, which parses `--opt` against every non-empty subset of the
seven listed kinds, in order and reversed, every spec named `opt`: the C's selected spec is the
first the Rust's predicate accepts, with the status that follows. That of the function goes
through `cli_opt_parser_init`'s `needs_sort`, for the four combinations of the style flags, each
beside none or three sets of unnamed bits, in three child environments. Mutating either port
(an accumulator as an option; `GNU` ignoring the variable) fails its equivalence test. The CLI
has no C tests to carry over. Worklist coverage: `opt.rs` 90 of 90 lines, 24 of 24 functions,
92 of 92 regions; C `support_gnu_style` every line, each branch reached, and the macro's line
of `spec_for_long` 224 times.

Coverage was measured with `crustify/scripts/coverage/run.sh` on this tree and read with
`report.py` from the scratch tree's `src/` (`C=@c` over the `coverage` variant's
`libcrustify.a`, `Rust=.`), the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`; the base is batch 0's
measurement of the tip it landed, recorded in `Coverage stats`, not measured again. The shifts
in suites whose new tests run no C (`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`) are run-to-run variation; `equiv`'s
`+0.12` pp C is the parser lines its new tests reach. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's
`code.loc.total` (`+695`, the regenerated bindings included) and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+226`).
`+LoC` counts every `.rs` line, `bindings.rs`'s 833 among them. `ported symbols` counts the two
items against the recorded total.

The safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, `--ffibox`, `--sys-crates pcre2_sys`, the 13 seams,
`--regions ffi_import,ffi_export`, no export feature in the manifest) is compared with batch 0's
scan of the tip. `ffimap api` against the tip, with ffibox's private rustdoc JSON (nightly
`2026-10-08`): both items are `new`; of the unattributed modules `sys::git2` is `extended`, the
other 18 `kept`.

Gates, all on the rebased tree (`8a149ac08` plus this batch): the workspace is formatted, and
`clippy --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. The whole workspace passes on `plain` (`lib`
844 and 1 ignored, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120, `equiv` 534, `unit_pub` 81, `hidden_symbols`
1, doctests 74 merged and 378 standalone). The module's tests (`lib` 4, `equiv` 6, `unit_pub`
14, doctests 2) pass under ASan+UBSan, and under Miri all but three, each run alone there and
seen to stop: the two child-process tests at `current_exe` (`spawns a process`) and the macro's
equivalence test at `cli_opt_parser_init` (`calls C`). The coverage runs ran every suite; only
the known `CommitBuilder` compile-fail doctest fails. TSan and BSan have no obligation: the
batch adds no unsafe code to the safe crate, no `Send` or `Sync` claim and no thread. The raw
bindings changed, so the crate was packaged in bundled mode and verified, by batch 0's command
(`crustify/evolution/packaging-gate-procedure`). Usage cells are the assistant's.
EOF

I've landed batch 1 on `crustify/waves/wave-186` as `29ec3ab87`, fast-forwarded on top of batch-0's `8a149ac08`, and released the landing lock.

**Both items do depend on batch-0's enums**, which the task assumed they didn't. The macro compares a spec's `type` with three `cli_opt_type_t` constants, and `support_gnu_style` tests two `cli_opt_flag_t` constants. Wavefront records neither edge; that gap is the existing `wavefront-enum-constant-uses` proposal, and `schedule.json` put them in one wave because of it. I didn't bind the enums myself. I developed against stand-ins copied from batch-0's in-progress `Kind` and `ParseFlags`, waited for it to land, then rebased onto its real types. That is why I landed second.

**What I ported**, into `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`:
- **`spec_is_option_type`** became `Kind::is_option()`, a `const fn` that is true only for `Bool`, `Switch` and `Value`. It takes the spec's kind rather than the spec, because the spec type itself is only wrapped in wave 187. The C parser has a branch for long accumulator options that this check makes unreachable. I kept that as the C has it, since no CLI spec is an accumulator.
- **`support_gnu_style`** became `uses_gnu_style(ParseFlags) -> bool`. rustdoc rejects a doc alias equal to the item's name, so I renamed it and kept the alias. Both items are `pub`, as earlier ports are. Nothing is exported, since no C outside `opt.c` uses either one.
- **Raw bindings:** I allowlisted `cli_opt_parser_init` and `cli_opt_parser_next` so the equivalence tests can reach the C, and regenerated `sys/git2/bindings.rs`.

**libc `getenv` confirmation:** `{batch: wave-186/batch-1, route: recommended, crate: std, rust_api: std::env::var_os, note: ""}`. It holds exactly: the C only checks whether `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set, so an empty value counts as set, which matches `var_os(..).is_some()`.

**Tests:**
- Six `unit_pub` tests and two doctests check the contracts. The `POSIXLY_CORRECT` cases run in child processes, because setting the environment is unsafe while the harness's threads run.
- Two `equiv` tests compare the ports with the C through the parser:
  - the macro, over every subset of the seven spec kinds, in order and reversed;
  - the function, by reading `needs_sort` for every flag combination, including unknown bits, with the variable unset, set and empty.
- I broke each port deliberately and the matching equivalence test failed both times.
- Coverage of `opt.rs` is 90/90 lines; every line of the C `support_gnu_style` is reached.

**Gates after the rebase:** I reran all of them on the rebased tree, so none could have gone stale.
- fmt and `clippy --all-targets` with warnings denied are clean.
- The whole workspace passes on `plain`: lib 844, ub_safe 762, ub_unsafe 120, equiv 534, unit_pub 81, hidden_symbols 1, doctests 74+378.
- The module's tests pass under ASan/UBSan. Under Miri all pass except three marked `ignore`, each seen to stop at a process spawn or a C call.
- The bundled-mode package builds and verifies.
- In the coverage run, only the known `CommitBuilder` compile-fail doctest fails.
- TSan and BSan don't apply: the batch adds no unsafe code to the safe crate, no `Send`/`Sync` claim and no thread.
- For the coverage and ffimap baselines I reused batch-0's measurements of the tip I rebased onto, rather than measuring that tree a second time.

**Safety audit:** the row shows `+10` public `unsafe fn`, `+30` raw dereferences and `+37` unsafe blocks. All of these are bindgen's bitfield helpers in the generated `sys/git2/bindings.rs`. The safe crate's own counts don't change. The dashboard rows and notes are filled; the usage cells are yours.

**Proposals and changes:**
- I filed `crustify/evolution/doc-alias-equal-to-the-name`, a change to the conventions' Anchors section that I can't make myself.
- I added this case as later evidence to `wavefront-enum-constant-uses`.
- I changed no skill.
